fixes.explanation: Divide sounds like trouble, but it's not the word Paul picks. Paul, the one writing this letter in chains, says his circumstances “…have actually served to advance the gospel.” He does talk about people preaching Christ out of envy and rivalry later on. Even there, he says Christ is preached.

False it is. Paul says most of the brothers are “…confident in the Lord by my chains, now dare more greatly to speak the word without fear.” So most of them weren't scared into silence. They were bolder, and I'd love to see that on a motivational poster.

Secret makes for a good spy movie, but it's not in the verse. Paul says they preach Christ “…in love, knowing that I am appointed for the defense of the gospel.” Love is the word the verse gives. That's what fills the blank.

This one is True, friend. Paul asks, “What then is the issue?” and he says, “Just this: that in every way, whether by false motives or true, Christ is preached.” He answers his own question in the same breath. What matters to him is that Christ is preached.

Paul says it will come “…through your prayers and the provision of the Spirit of Jesus Christ…” So the Philippians' prayers are part of this. And the Spirit's provision is right there next to them. Two things, side by side.

I can see why you'd read it that way, since staying alive makes the exalting easier to picture. But Paul says he eagerly expects and hopes that Christ will be exalted in his body, “…whether by life or by death.” Both are covered. So it's not only if he keeps on living.
Paul asks, “So what shall I choose?” and then answers, “I do not know.” That's an honest answer. He says he is torn between the two. Paul doesn't pretend to have it all figured out.

True. Paul says, “Convinced of this, I know that I will remain and will continue with all of you for your progress and joy in the faith…” Back in verse 22 he said, “I do not know.” Now he says he knows. Keep up, friend.

That's it, friend. Paul says, “Nevertheless, conduct yourselves in a manner worthy of the gospel of Christ.” Then he says he wants to know they stand firm whether he comes and sees them or only hears about them in his absence. It's like doing good work whether the boss is watching or not. He wants their living to match the gospel either way.

Paul wants to know they “…stand firm in one spirit, contending together as one for the faith of the gospel.” Think of a tug-of-war team, everybody pulling the same direction. That's the picture of contending together as one. And it starts with one spirit.

I can see why it might seem like theirs is a different road. But Paul says, “…you are encountering the same struggle you saw I had, and now hear that I still have.” Same struggle, not a different one. So this one is False.
